title: DCC-GARCH(1,1) for SPY-GLD Dynamic Correlation
method: Two-step: (1) GJR-GARCH for SPY + GARCH for GLD → standardized residuals, (2) DCC QML estimation
key_findings: DCC parameters both highly significant (a: t=5.83, b: t=111.60)
DCC significantly better than CCC (LR=88.39, p<1e-6)
Ljung-Box on DCC residuals: Q(10)=6.43, p=0.78 → model adequate
2-asset risk parity: correlation cancels analytically (w1*sigma1 = w2*sigma2)
MVP with DCC: Sharpe=1.753, MVP with rho=0: Sharpe=1.810 → difference NOT significant (p=0.30)
Target-vol DCC reduces vol-of-vol by 14% vs naive (0.0164 vs 0.0191)
VaR 1% with DCC: 1.40% exceedance (Kupiec p=0.40, PASS)
VaR 1% with rho=0: 2.40% exceedance (Kupiec p=0.008, FAIL)
DCC improves risk measurement but NOT portfolio allocation for 2-asset case
conclusion: DCC-GARCH captures statistically significant time-varying correlation for SPY-GLD. However, for 2-asset risk parity, correlation cancels analytically. For MVP, the improvement is not statistically significant. The main practical value is in VaR estimation: DCC-based VaR passes Kupiec test (1.40% vs expected 1%) while naive fails (2.40%). Recommendation: use DCC for risk measurement/VaR, but inverse-vol weights remain optimal for 2-asset allocation.

VVIX alone does NOT predict VaR violations (OOS AUC=0.44, worse than random). VIX/GARCH ratio remains the dominant predictor (AUC=0.76). VVIX adds no incremental info (LR p=0.61). However, combined rule VVIX>100 & VIX/GARCH>1.5 achieves 3.31x lift, capturing 58.3% violations in 17.6% of days — but this is driven by VIX/GARCH, not VVIX.

title: VIX Proxy Transport Cross-Market Test
description: Test K/VIX VT strategy for 7 assets (SPY, EFA, EEM, FXI, EWJ, 0050.TW, IWM). Sweep K=4-20, OOS 2016-2025, monthly rebalancing with lagged VIX.
result: K is irrelevant for Sharpe (linear leverage identity). VIX timing alpha: SPY +0.028, FXI +0.039, 0050.TW +0.062 (works); EFA -0.070, EEM -0.149, EWJ -0.021, IWM -0.097 (fails). MDD improvement universal 10-16%. Cross-validation shows timing alpha sign unstable. Predictive regression insignificant for all assets.

config.strategy_a: GARCH-budget (GJR for SPY, GARCH for GLD/TLT)

conclusions: GARCH risk budgeting Sharpe 0.791 vs RV22 0.771 — delta +0.021, NOT significant (p=0.748)
Both dynamic methods NOT significant vs Static (p>0.89)
GARCH has LOWER turnover than RV22 (14.6% vs 17.9%) — smoother weights
GARCH won COVID sub-period (Sharpe 1.59 vs 1.21), RV22 won rate hikes and recovery
Confirms complexity ceiling: forward-looking GARCH adds negligible value over simple RV22 for risk budgeting
Sub-period winners rotate: Static (pre-COVID), GARCH (COVID), RV22 (rate hikes, recovery)

title: CNN Fear & Greed Index vs VT Strategy
hypothesis: CNN Fear & Greed Index provides incremental information beyond VIX for VT strategy overlays and return prediction
method: Three experiments: (A) FG-based VT overlay (18/VIX in fear, 8/VIX in greed), (B) FG→volatility prediction with VIX control, (C) FG→return prediction with VIX control

exp_B.verdict: REDUNDANT - economically negligible after VIX control

exp_C.verdict: WEAK/NULL - contrarian signal exists but no increment over VIX

conclusion: CNN Fear & Greed Index is approximately a rescaled inverse VIX composite. It provides NO incremental value for VT strategy overlays. VIX alone captures all useful information.

title: Shiller CAPE as vol/return predictor
hypothesis: CAPE > 30 predicts higher future volatility and lower returns
method: Pearson/Spearman correlation, partial correlation (ctrl VIX), regime analysis, quintile sort, multivariate regression, VT overlay backtest with OOS split
result: NULL — CAPE raw r=-0.22 with fwd vol vanishes to r=0.00 after controlling VIX. CAPE adds zero incremental R² over VIX alone. Return prediction also NS (r=-0.10, p=0.097). CAPE VT overlay shows modest MDD improvement but no Sharpe improvement.
conclusion: CAPE is redundant for volatility prediction when VIX is available. Not useful as a standalone signal. May have marginal value as MDD-reducing overlay via CAPE Step rule.

title: Overnight vs Intraday Vol Decomposition
hypothesis: Intraday returns predict next-day vol better than overnight returns
method: Decompose SPY log returns into overnight=ln(open/prev_close) and intraday=ln(close/open). Compare Spearman rho with next-day Parkinson RV. GJR-GARCH on intraday-only vs total returns (rolling OOS).

title: Overnight Gap as VT Signal
hypothesis: Adding overnight gap penalty to 12/VIX VT improves risk-adjusted returns
method: Compare 12/VIX baseline, 12/VIX+gap adjustment, pure overnight vol VT. F-test for gap info beyond VIX. Regression: next-day RV ~ VIX + |overnight gap|.

title: Range-Based Vol Estimators Comparison
hypothesis: Range-based estimators outperform squared returns for vol forecasting
method: Compare Parkinson, Garman-Klass, Yang-Zhang vs squared returns. Spearman at 1/5/10/22d horizons, QLIKE vs GJR-GARCH forecast, efficiency ratios, DM test.
